gen-gf-warnes-gf-lexend-mega: Expressive and loud, Warnes tapers its ink strokes to points. Lexend Mega is the plain sans that takes over for the talking, wide and uniform, every letter drawn as if with a single nib.
gen-irish-grover-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta brings big, round curves that never thin out, with a wide-mouthed c. Irish Grover is the fun, sturdy-looking heading above it, so give it a larger size and let the body sit a step down.
gen-megrim-gf-lexend-zetta: Hairline-sharp and angular, Megrim holds every stroke at one measured thickness, which gives headings a futuristic edge. And Lexend Zetta carries the text in tall-bodied, widely tracked letters cut like ribbon, friendly where the heading is severe.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-montserrat-alternat: Open jaws on every curve give Mystery Quest a bookish, nostalgic look with compact ascenders. Montserrat Alternates follows with round letters whose rims match their stems, so the old-fashioned heading gets a contemporary, chalk-board-tall partner below.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-lexend-exa: Pixel-pinned and playful, Press Start 2P spaces its letters far apart like cut-outs. And Lexend Exa, a sans-serif of constant-thickness tubing with wide curves, is what makes the retro heading feel anchored.
gen-righteous-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga spreads its flat, single-weight linework with generous tracking, and its ascenders barely clear the x-height. And Righteous, bent like thin steel rod with bowls that fill the line, handles the commanding heading work above it.
gen-tourney-gf-lexend-mega: Bold and athletic, Tourney cuts every stroke to one width and stretches its words wide with bulky small letters. Lexend Mega feels friendlier beside it.
gen-almendra-display-bitter: Bitter reads grounded and dependable, with a large lowercase eye. Its slab-serif sturdiness against the ornate, literary Almendra Display is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-audiowide-gf-montserrat-alternates: Montserrat Alternates crowds its chalk-board lowercase up toward the capital line. Against Audiowide's tile-like glyphs and wide gaps, that tight, round-rimmed sans-serif is where the pair gets its futuristic polish.
gen-eater-gf-lexend-zetta: Aggressive and dark, Eater pairs thin strokes with moderately weighty stems. Lexend Zetta runs over a longer stretch like glass tubing, hollow, constant in width and widely tracked, so the sans body stays approachable.
